title: Game creation with a single prompt—next step after large language models?
author: minemateinnovation
selftext:
I’m fascinated by how **OpenAI** has led the charge in text generation, and now I’m seeing new AI tools go in all sorts of directions. A platform called [Degs.ai](http://degs.ai) caught my eye—it basically applies a prompt-based approach to **casual game dev**. You describe the game, and it spits out a working prototype in minutes.  

I tried something silly like “Make a platformer where you’re a chicken running from space aliens,” and sure enough, it generated a functional, though rudimentary, platformer. The interface is simple: you can sign up with just an email, no need to do anything blockchain-related unless you want to. They also give **20 free daily builds**, so it’s easy to play around.  

It makes me wonder: could we see more specialized “GPT-like” tools that produce entire interactive apps or games based on user requests? Right now, it’s definitely not AAA quality, but it’s decent enough for quick prototypes or casual titles. Imagine if these systems improve at the same pace we’ve seen with text generation.  

If anyone else has tried it, I’d love to know what you think. Are we on the verge of AI-based game studios becoming the norm?
